newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Dozens of Hutus suffocated in Zaire refugee train.
newsitem.headline: Dozens of Hutus suffocated in Zaire refugee train.

text.p: Dozens of Rwandan Hutu refugees were suffocated or crushed to death on Sunday in a train carrying them from a refugee camp in Zaire to be repatriated by air.

Aid workers and journalists saw dozens of bodies of refugees tumbling from open railway carriages as a train carrying them from Biaro, 41 kms (25 miles) away, pulled into Kisangani station in northeastern Zaire.
An official of the United Nation refugee agency UNHCR said he estimated more than 100 people had died in the crush.
The train pulled into Kisangani shortly after 5 p.m. (1700 GMT). Aid officials had been told by Zairean rebel authorities who control the railway to expect around 2,800 refugees.
It was clear that the six open-topped carriages carried hundreds more, and the dead came tumbling out as those packed inside still living leapt over the sides as the train came to a stop.
The refugees are part of over 80,000 Rwandan Hutus camped south of Kisangani awaiting a United Nations airlift to take them home.
